From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T16:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Unexpected 429s from morning run

Checked infra and rate-limiter configs. Root cause summary: per-tenant quota mapping for Acme (org: acme-123) was accidentally mapped to a shared config profile due to a recent rollout of routing policy v3.0. The shared profile had a lower per-second token rate (intended for sandbox/test tenants). When a second large customer hit steady traffic at 09:03 PT, the shared bucket hit capacity and started returning 429s for others mapped to that bucket (including Acme).

Mitigation performed (09:12–09:20 PT):
- Temporarily increased per-tenant token rate for acme-123 to restore capacity (rolled at 09:12).
- Reverted the erroneous mapping in the routing policy and re-deployed v3.0 with the corrected tenant map at 09:18.
- Warmed KV cache and restarted a small subset of serving workers for the route to clear burst backpressure (09:20).

Status: traffic normalized by 09:23 PT and error rate dropped to baseline. We captured timeline and key logs (see incident_timeline.txt).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Audit routing-policy rollout automation to ensure tenant mappings are validated pre-deploy.
2) Add a canary check that simulates a high-throughput tenant against new routing configs.
3) Provide Acme with the incident timeline and remediation steps + offer a one-time unit credit.

Attaching: incident_timeline.txt (internal).

Rohan
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-08T17:06:00-07:00
Subject: Post-incident update — 429s earlier today (Acme Analytics)

Hi Julia — following up with a short technical summary and remediation plan. Thank you for the quick report and the request IDs — they helped us trace the timeline.

What happened (TL;DR): A routing-policy rollout accidentally mapped Acme's tenant id to a shared test profile with a lower per-second quota. This caused temporary cross-tenant exhaustion when another customer produced a burst. We identified the misconfiguration, increased Acme's effective token rate, and corrected the policy. Normal service resumed by ~09:23 PT.

What we did (timeline):
- 09:03 PT: Surge from another tenant observed; 429s start for the affected bucket.
- 09:12 PT: SRE applied a temporary per-tenant increase for acme-123.
- 09:18 PT: Fixed routing-policy mapping and re-deployed v3.0 with validated tenant map.
- 09:20 PT: Warmed caches + restarted a small set of workers; 429s fall back to baseline by 09:23 PT.

Impact: ~20 minutes of elevated 429s, ~18% error rate for a narrow time window affecting some of your ingestion jobs. No data exfiltration; no request bodies were dropped — all affected requests returned 429s only.

Remediation & recommended actions for Acme:
- We have attached a remediation_steps.md that includes temporary client-side retry guidance (backoff + jitter) and a short checklist for integrating rate limit headers into your ingest pipeline.
- We'll run a targeted audit of your tenant mapping and confirm the commit history for the routing-policy rollout.
- As a gesture of goodwill we’ll issue a one-time service credit for the affected token billing window. I’ll loop legal/billing if you want formal credit details.

Attachments: remediation_steps.md, postmortem_summary.pdf

Please let me know if you want a quick call with Rohan and the SREs to walk through the technical details; we can do 30 minutes tomorrow.

Best,
Marissa
